screens.title: High-rate qLDPC processors
screens.version: arXiv:2607.28795v1, 30 July 2026; internal manuscript date 24 August 2026
screens.method: Searched all text for conjecture/question/unknown/future/remaining/direction terms; reviewed introduction, conclusion, relevant theorem proofs and all candidate contexts; checked later same-text resolution.
screens.result: Broad directions extracted; no additional numbered conjecture identified.
screens.comparison: Appendix G, Theorem 8 and Lemmas 5–6 give an upper bound under full binary row rank. Remark 12 shows the rank premise cannot generally be dropped. This is not the lower bound needed for equality in F25; fully populated monomial 3x4 bases are rank deficient at augmentation.

screens.title: Lifting Lifted Product Codes
screens.version: arXiv:2607.28621v1, 30 July 2026; internal manuscript date 24 August 2026
screens.method: Searched all text for conjecture/question/unknown/future/remaining/direction terms; reviewed introduction, conclusion, relevant theorem proofs and all candidate contexts; checked later same-text resolution.
screens.result: Broad directions extracted; no additional numbered conjecture identified.
screens.comparison: Section II and Corollary 6 describe compatible group-extension lifts and chain/cochain transfer. For odd lift index, d_lift<=t*d_base; the reverse inequality stated there additionally assumes unchanged logical dimension. This does not settle our classical-distance versus quantum-distance equality question. Our candidate family has growing logical dimension.
